lede: The story of Christmas in Princeton runs from a railroad switch on the Wilson brothers' farm, where trains arrived in 1881, to Merry Moments, the city's string of December pop up parties. The city lit its tree at Veterans Memorial Park in 2021, and today Santa, reindeer and hot chocolate turn up on weeknights all month.
celebrates: Princeton Parks and Recreation runs Merry Moments, a series of festive pop up events through December. The city lists a Deck the Halls Dash on the Municipal Park trail, Selfies with Santa at the Municipal Center, Holiday Hero Headquarters with superhero capes, Beanie and Bright, Reindeer Magic with a real reindeer, and Blue Lights and Bright Nights with the Princeton Police Department. Merry on Main St. fills Veterans Memorial Park on parade night. The fire department hosts Pancakes with Santa at Fire Station 2, and Santa's mailbox sits at three city buildings. Outside town, Cathy's Critters opens its farm for a holiday vendor fair.

By 2026 the city had grown its December into Merry Moments, which its sponsorship packet describes as two weeks of holiday magic with festive activities, entertainment, Santa experiences and family fun.
facts: Princeton almost had a different name. The area was known as Wilson's Switch after farmers T. B. and George Wilson, but when residents applied for a post office the name Wilson was taken, so they chose Princeton after landowner Prince Dowlin. The post office opened in 1888. The town later held a lumber factory that became the state's largest producer of bois d'arc lumber, and during World War II it housed a prisoner of war camp.
trains: Princeton began beside the tracks. In 1881 the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railroad extended its line from Greenville to McKinney through land the Wilson brothers owned, and the stop became Wilson's Switch. There is no passenger rail in Princeton today. The closest DART light rail is Parker Road Station in Plano, the northern end of the Red and Orange lines. Amtrak's Texas Eagle and the TRE leave from Dallas Union Station, and the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano shows Texas Electric Railway Car 360.

sections: From Wilson's Switch to Princeton, 1881 to 1888

Princeton started as a railroad stop. In the late 1870s T. B. Wilson and his brother George farmed near the future townsite, and in 1881 the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railroad built its line from Greenville to McKinney across their land. People called the spot Wilson's Switch. When residents asked for a post office, they learned the name Wilson was already in use, so they sent in Princeton to honor Prince Dowlin, a landowner who promoted the town. The post office opened in 1888, and the farm town grew around grain elevators, mills and onion fields on the Blackland Prairie.
Merry Moments, Princeton's December of pop ups

Instead of one big night, Princeton Parks and Recreation spreads Christmas across December with Merry Moments. The city's page lists a Deck the Halls Dash with cookie decorating at Princeton Municipal Park, Selfies with Santa at the Municipal Center, superhero capes at Holiday Hero Headquarters, beanie decorating at Beanie and Bright, a real reindeer at Reindeer Magic and story time with SWAT at Blue Lights and Bright Nights. Merry on Main St. brings a silent disco and face painting to Veterans Memorial Park, and Cocoa, Candy Canes and Cheer ends the run at Public Works with an obstacle course.

The tracks that made Wilson's Switch still mark Princeton's past, but families who want a train ride at Christmas drive west. DART's Red and Orange lines end at Parker Road Station in Plano, about a half hour away, and from there light rail runs into Dallas. Dallas Union Station serves Amtrak's Texas Eagle and the Trinity Railway Express. In downtown Plano, the Interurban Railway Museum displays Texas Electric Railway Car 360, built in 1911, a reminder of the electric interurban line that once carried Collin County families to Dallas.

kidfact: Princeton is named after a man called Prince. The town wanted to be called Wilson, but that name was taken, so it picked Princeton for landowner Prince Dowlin.
faq: What are Merry Moments in Princeton?

Merry Moments is the City of Princeton's series of festive pop up events in December, run by Parks and Recreation. Each evening has a theme, from Selfies with Santa at the Municipal Center to Reindeer Magic at Princeton Municipal Park, and most include crafts and a hot chocolate bar while supplies last. The city posts the full list on its Merry Moments page.
Where can kids mail a letter to Santa in Princeton?

The city sets out Santa's mailbox at three places: Parks and Recreation at 306 N. Main Street, the Lois Nelson Public Library at 323 McKinney Avenue and the Princeton Municipal Center at 2000 E. Princeton Drive. Children who drop off a letter get a special reply from Santa, according to the city.
How did Princeton, Texas get its name?

The area was first called Wilson's Switch, after farmers T. B. and George Wilson, whose land the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railroad crossed in 1881. The name Wilson was already used by another post office, so residents chose Princeton to honor landowner Prince Dowlin. The Princeton post office opened in 1888.

Princeton has grown quickly. The Texas Almanac lists 3,477 residents in 2000, 6,807 in 2010 and 17,027 at the 2020 census, then an estimate of 20,046 for 2021. That puts it well over 20,000 people today, up from about 500 in the 1920s.
Is there a train near Princeton, Texas?

Not in town. The closest DART light rail station is Parker Road Station in Plano, the northern end of the Red and Orange lines. Dallas Union Station has Amtrak's Texas Eagle and the Trinity Railway Express, and the Interurban Railway Museum in downtown Plano shows a restored interurban car.
